newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies seen up sharply on Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies seen up sharply on Taiwan.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open 0.500 to 1.250 cent per lb higher while pork belly futures were called 0.500 to 2.00 cent a lb higher, livestock analysts said.

Leftover buy stops after futures posted limit gains for the second straight day Friday in April through August hog futures and May pork bellies should boost hog and belly futures at the start. The market is still being driven up by ideas U.S. pork exports will increase sharply to fill the need for pork resulting from Taiwan's suspension of pork exports, they said.
Speculation is, it could be a year or more before the foot and mouth disease is cleared up there and Taiwanese exports resume.

A large part of Taiwan's pork sales to Japan and South Korea will likely be filled by U.S. pork, analysts said, and pork values have already started to rise as packers increase supplies to meet anticipated demand. The Taiwan problem also was expected to overshadow a bearish USDA Cold Storage report Friday, they said.
Thursday's quarterly USDA Hog and Pigs report will have to show increased hog numbers to provide any resistance to these markets, analysts added.
Analysts' estimates on the report ranged from 97 to 100.6 percent of a year ago for all U.S. hogs.
Hogs kept for breeding were seen at 98.5 to 104 percent of a year ago and hogs kept for market 97 to 100.8 percent.
